clue.text: Sorting out theft, lawman short of a stand by

indicators.note: sorting out a jumble of letters puts them into a new order, so the following words are rearranged
short of means lacking, so one letter is dropped from the word before it

explanation.surface: A detective puts a robbery case in order, though the lawman is not quite at full strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of a' takes A from LAWMAN, leaving LWMAN; 'Sorting out' rearranges THEFT plus LWMAN. In cricket the twelfth man is the reserve player who fields for an injured team-mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side's reserve player is its standby, ready to come on as a substitute fielder.

clue.text: Playfully, require nothing but …

parts.note: to require something is to want it
nothing but means only, as in 'only water'

explanation.surface: Someone asks, half in jest, to have nothing but one thing, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 3 Down for the surface only; each is solved on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting wantonly can mean acting frivolously or in sport, without serious purpose.

clue.text: … convenience in game

definitions.meaning: a public convenience is a lavatory, British slang for which is this word
also the name of an old card game played for stakes

explanation.surface: Completing 2 Down: a playful wish for nothing but some convenience during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A loo is a British lavatory, and loo is also a historic trick-taking card game.

clue.text: Shrinking cotton fabric shrunk up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
shrunk means made shorter, so the last letter of the fabric is cut off

parts.note: dimity is a light, striped cotton fabric

explanation.surface: A cotton garment has shrunk and ridden up after washing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrunk' trims DIMITY to DIMIT; 'up' turns it round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinking as an adjective describes someone shy and retiring, as in a shrinking violet.

clue.text: Polo taken to Northern Ireland by inventor

parts.note: Marco Polo was the Venetian traveller, so his first name stands for Polo

explanation.surface: A game of polo is being introduced to Northern Ireland by some ingenious person.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo looks like the sport, but it leads to the explorer Marco Polo.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi was the Italian inventor credited with pioneering radio telegraphy.

clue.text: Don't concern yourself with Edward, the rat-catcher

indicators.note: a catcher holds something within it, so the name is wrapped around the creature

parts.note: Ned is a familiar form of the name Edward
rats are classed as vermin

explanation.surface: Someone is told not to worry about Edward, the local rat-catcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat-catcher' looks like a trade describing Edward, but the hyphenated word splits: 'catcher' is the container signal holding the rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Never mind is an idiom telling someone not to bother or worry about something.

clue.text: I have bad habits, and incline to scratch

definitions.meaning: a dissolute pleasure-seeking man might say this of himself
the slope of a theatre stage is called this
to drag something with teeth or claws across a surface

explanation.surface: A confession of vice, followed by a tendency to scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute man, a stage's slope, and to rake is to scratch or scrape.

clue.text: Ending in debt, Roger and Madge, distraught, borrowed more money

indicators.note: distraught means in turmoil, so these letters are thrown into disorder
ending in picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Roger and Madge, deep in debt and frantic, borrowed again against their house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ending in debt' gives T; 'distraught' rearranges T with ROGER and MADGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To remortgage is to take out a further loan secured on property, borrowing more.

clue.text: More devoted person mourning

definitions.meaning: more eager or enthusiastic, comparative of keen
someone who wails a lament for the dead, especially at an Irish funeral

explanation.surface: A grieving mourner shows greater devotion than others.
explanation.definitionFit: Keener is the comparative of keen, and also an Irish term for a professional wailer at funerals.

clue.text: Grass all the rage in the past

parts.note: something all the rage is in fashion, or simply in
former describes what was so in the past

explanation.surface: A lawn that was fashionable long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass looks like the lawn, but here it is slang for someone who tells the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is British slang for a police informant, someone who betrays others.

clue.text: Five in the morning, and quiet editor is seduced

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
a.m. marks times in the morning
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: At five a.m. a quiet editor is being tempted by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To vamp is to seduce or beguile someone, from the femme fatale type called a vamp.

clue.text: Gruesome globe put in, in the middle of …

indicators.note: put in tells us the sphere is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: mid means in the middle of, as in midstream
an orb is a globe, as in the royal orb

explanation.surface: A grisly scene in which a globe is placed in the centre of something, continued in the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Morbid means having an unhealthy interest in death or gruesome things.

clue.text: Took robbing badly, delivering reprimand

indicators.note: badly signals that the preceding words are done wrongly, so their letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone made a poor job of a robbery and was given a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone to book is to make them answer for their conduct, a formal reprimand.

clue.text: … models of solar system — ie errors get made

indicators.note: the errors are remade into something new, so their letters form a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Model planetaria are made where mistakes get made.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model showing the planets moving around the sun.

clue.text: Steppes under the weather provide easy progress

parts.note: steppes are vast grassy plains of Eurasia
feeling under the weather means unwell, ailing

explanation.surface: Bad weather over the steppes makes a journey across them easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain sailing is an idiom for a straightforward course free of difficulties.

clue.text: Another name is therefore given to fuel

parts.note: so means therefore, as in 'and so'
a briquet, or briquette, is a block of compressed coal dust used as fuel

explanation.surface: Fuel acquires a different name for that reason.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobriquet is a nickname, an alternative name given to someone.

clue.text: Two passes, and fold

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountains
a lapse is a passing of time, as when a period lapses

explanation.surface: A card player passes twice and then folds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests poker; the 'passes' are a mountain pass and time passing.
explanation.definitionFit: To fold can mean to collapse or give way, as a failing business folds.

clue.text: Having eaten fast, I give approval to mumbo-jumbo

parts.note: to gobble is to eat greedily and fast
ego is Latin for I, the self
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: After wolfing down a meal, someone endorses some nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobbledegook is pompous, unintelligible jargon, the same as mumbo-jumbo.

clue.text: Upbringing fixed genuine character in Hamlet

indicators.note: read as bringing up: in a down clue the letters are lifted so they read upwards

parts.note: set means fixed, as in a set price
real means genuine

explanation.surface: A rigid upbringing produced someone of real character, in a review of Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upbringing' looks like childhood, but it is 'bringing up': SETREAL read backwards in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes is Polonius's son and Ophelia's brother in Shakespeare's Hamlet.

clue.text: Measure round book

parts.note: a quart is a measure of liquid, two pints
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A measurement taken around a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarto is a book size made by folding sheets twice into four leaves.

clue.text: Assumed diamonds to be shelved

parts.note: to assume a manner is to put it on
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Diamonds are taken for granted and then set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put on ice are postponed or set aside, just as shelved ones are.

clue.text: Pleasure boat limped along to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A boat for leisure hobbled along a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedalo is a small pleasure craft driven by pedals, hired at seasides and lakes.

clue.text: Something of David's secreted initially in one's hand

indicators.note: in places the single letter within the hand

parts.note: the palm is the inside of one's hand

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: Something belonging to David was hidden in someone's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S from 'secreted'. King David is traditionally the author of many of the Psalms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Psalms are traditionally ascribed to King David, so a psalm is one of his compositions.

clue.text: Alloy of gold originally making ornaments look unique

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A golden alloy that makes decorations look one of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is a gilded bronze or brass alloy used to decorate furniture and clocks.

clue.text: Various patterns appear in part of church

indicators.note: various suggests different forms, so the letters take another arrangement

explanation.surface: Different designs show up in a section of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The transept is the cross arm of a church, crossing the nave at right angles.

clue.text: One interesting the police in slums regularly

indicators.note: regularly picks letters at even intervals, here every other one starting with the first

explanation.surface: Someone in the slums who keeps attracting police attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Sus is British slang for a suspect, someone the police are interested in.

clue.text: Rugby player has to secure hair

definitions.meaning: a second-row forward in rugby union
a strand or tress of hair

explanation.surface: A rugby player has to tie back his hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Lock names a second-row rugby forward, a fastening, and a tress of hair.

clue.text: Demand money at first during brief experience as a slave-driver

indicators.note: during means within, so these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: a taster is a short sample or brief experience of something
to demand is to ask

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Someone demands money up front during a short trial as a harsh overseer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes M from 'money'; ASKM goes inside TASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A taskmaster is a demanding supervisor who drives others hard, a slave-driver.
